correctness.limitations: The statement applies only to real eigenpairs with nonzero z in the kernel of scaled C. Exact formulas above give the continuous witness and equality case; rational spot checks are corroborative. No claim is made about all eigenvalues, convergence or arbitrarily prescribed randomized Q.
correctness.rationale: Conjugating the generalized pencil by the inverse square roots gives the stated equations. With Cz=0 in scaled coordinates the first and third equations give x*Ãx=λ(||x||²+||z||²); x=0 would force z=0 by injectivity of the scaled B transpose. Hence 0<λ<b strictly. If λ<a, eliminating x and using the inverse Loewner order gives λ≥β/(b−λ), equivalently λ(b−λ)≥β. The discriminant and lower-root cases follow only on λ<a, and the complementary branch λ≥a yields the clipping. When the root r exists, r=β/(b−r)≥β/b, which also gives the weaker universally clipped bound. To verify the full asserted attainment regime r≤a, take A=diag(a,b,b), B with rows √β e2^T and √β e3^T, C=(0,1), identity approximating blocks and any positive E; y=0,z=e1,x=−√β e2/(b−r) is an eigenvector at r by r(b−r)=β, even at r=a. In the proposed unbounded family, s²=3+6t² gives Bx=(2t²−s²/3)e1=−e1 and (A−I)x=−B^T z, so λ=1 for all t≥1. The Gram entries are 3+7t²,100t²,100t²; the first is the minimum and β/b diverges, with diagonal blocks fixed and all ranks and positivity requirements satisfied. Independent rational spot checks give β/b=10/7 and 850/7 at t=1 and t=11. These examples also satisfy the source paper's spectral-straddling normalization and avoid both diagonal spectra at λ=1.

value.rationale: The claimed lower enclosure of a concrete preconditioned branch can be wrong by an arbitrarily large factor even with diagonal spectra unchanged. Pinpointing the resolvent error and replacing the false inequality with a bound valid under the actual hypotheses is useful for interpreting those spectra. Attainability makes the quadratic portion meaningful, not merely a loose rescue.
